questions.question_en: A species is Data Deficient. What is the safest conclusion?
questions.question_te: Data Deficient speciesపై సరైన conclusion ఏది?
options: It has no habitat needs
There is insufficient evidence for the risk assessment; it is not proof of safety
It is certainly abundant and secure
It is already extinct by definition
option_explanations: All species have ecological requirements.
Missing data are an uncertainty, not a low-risk finding.
That conclusion is not justified.
Extinction is a different category.

questions.question_en: Why cannot a zoo population alone solve a species' conservation problem?
questions.question_te: Zoo population ఒక్కటే conservation సమస్యను ఎందుకు పరిష్కరించదు?
options: Natural habitat, genetic viability and ecological threats still need attention
All ecosystems are identical
Wild populations never need habitat
Captive breeding always removes every threat
option_explanations: Ex-situ tools complement rather than replace landscape conservation.
Habitat requirements differ.
Habitat is essential to wild populations.
Many threats remain outside captivity.

questions.question_en: Which statement about conservation labels is correct?
questions.question_te: Conservation labelsపై సరైనది ఏది?
options: A designation proves perfect management
Threat category, legal protection and international site recognition are different dimensions
Every Ramsar site is automatically the same as a national park
Endemic always means extinct
option_explanations: Implementation effectiveness needs evidence.
Different systems can overlap but answer different questions.
Categories/designations are not identical.
Endemism concerns range restriction.
